A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CCR framework, with matching core algorithms, simulations, and language-model experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison; v1's experimental Appendix F becomes Appendix G in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original CandyParty experiments with seven language-model architectures in Section 6 and Appendix F, plus finite-sample causal simulations in Appendices C and E.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and simulations and adds statistical findings, GPT-4o response analyses, and numerical CCT path-count illustrations.

M1.justification: v3 adds an automated task-generation component where v1 proposed automated task design as future work. Appendix F specifies random DAG/CCT construction, configurable graph complexity, randomized causal functions, prompt generation, and sampling for CandyParty and FlowerGarden. This substantially extends task construction, while Algorithm 1's evaluation steps remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same CandyParty task and retain the same causal simulation settings. FlowerGarden and variable graph structures are illustrated as generator capabilities in v3, without reported language-model evaluations on those additional tasks.

E2.justification: The seven evaluated architectures and their reported CoT comparisons are retained. Although v3 newly names o1 in the CoT experimental-design prose, o1 CoT already appears in v1's Figure 7 and appendix results. Table A.1 adds a literature capability comparison, not additional baseline experiments.

E3.justification: Appendix D adds a supplementary enumeration of CCTs with 3–11 nodes to examine path-count scaling. The existing LM task, model configurations, sampling budgets, RAE metric, and validity thresholds remain unchanged. The fuller CoT prompt and subsampling description clarify existing experiments rather than establish revised settings.

E4.justification: v3 adds four GPT-4o CoT case studies examining incorrect causal-parent extraction, faulty logic, and truncated reasoning (Figures G.7–G.10). Appendix D also adds numerical illustrations of exponential path growth. Earlier Llama error cases, mediation analyses, and finite-sample simulations are retained.

E5.justification: v3 adds Wilcoxon comparisons of CoT and non-CoT error distributions at alpha = 0.05. Appendix G.1 also explains the 1000 repeated subsamples drawn from five responses per question. v1 already reported 1000 PNS estimates and standard deviations; the added explanation does not establish more independent runs.

E6.justification: Matched benchmark scores remain unchanged: GPT-4o CoT has 95.67% composition validity and 77.76% local validity in both versions' corresponding appendix plots. v3 adds the finding that CoT error distributions differ significantly except for o1 on PNSXY, additional qualitative failure examples, and CCT path-count entries.

T1.justification: Assumption A4 changes from excluding observed and unobserved confounders for X,Y to excluding unobserved confounders for queried pairs. Appendix D specifies k = 2^(n−2) and an exponential error-count bound. Appendix B.2 also adds an incorrect assertion that monotonicity implies P(y'_x) = P(z'_y) = 0; the principal composition equations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Section 1.1 adds scalable, open-source qualitative and quantitative task generation as an explicit contribution, replacing v1's future-work aspiration. The central claims about CCR, the reasoning taxonomy, the evaluation framework, and the observed model-performance patterns remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 6.2 expands explanations of GPT-4o failures and why internal consistency distinguishes otherwise similar accuracy profiles, including a consistently biased IC reasoner. Section 6.3 adds implications for smaller/open models and interprets o1's success as validating implementation. The limitation to one illustrative LM task is retained.

D1.justification: v3 supplies an access link and reports release of the automated generator, documents its controls and randomization, explains how repeated subsampling produces PNS distributions, and prints the complete two-example CoT wrapper. These substantially expand reproducibility information beyond v1's release promises and abbreviated descriptions; model identifiers and hardware remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds an extensive comparison across commonsense, causal-relation extraction, and formal causal-reasoning frameworks, supported by numerous additional citations. Table A.1 and the CLADDER discussion substantially sharpen positioning around compositionality, graph scaling, internal consistency, and direct versus downstream causal inference.

P1.justification: v3 locally reorganizes Section 4 around obtaining estimates and measuring consistency, revises the experimental exposition and discussion, and moves limitations from Section 7 to Section 6.3. A generator appendix is inserted and the experimental appendix reorganized, while the overall narrative and much existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables A.1 and D.1, composition and scaling diagrams, illustrated generator prompts, and GPT-4o response figures. The former Figure 9 becomes a substantially redesigned Figure 8, displaying local/global validity and composition paths with new visual encodings. Figure 7 is recolored, while most benchmark plots retain their content.

improvement.justification: v3 improves practical reproducibility through explicit subsampling instructions, the complete CoT prompt, and documented task generation, while strengthening diagnostic discussion and research positioning. The core empirical coverage and scores remain unchanged. These gains are tempered by the new incorrect monotonicity explanation in Appendix B.2, supporting a limited overall improvement.
